subject.title: [do not merge] refactor: flip sessions and transcripts to sqlite storage

question: Should the one-way SQLite session/transcript migration, removal of active file-shaped Plugin SDK APIs, and documented downgrade limitations become the supported core upgrade contract in the next release?
rationale: Repository architecture favors SQLite-only canonical state, but accepting irreversible persisted-state migration, external API removal, rollback limitations, and operator recovery requirements is a maintainer product and compatibility choice that tests alone cannot settle.

options.title: Approve after all gates
options.body: Accept the one-way contract after unrelated changes and exact-head defects are removed and final-head upgrade, restart, continuity, archive, recovery, and downgrade proof is published.

options.title: Stage the compatibility break
options.body: Split the runtime storage flip from Plugin SDK removals or other irreversible compatibility changes so each contract can be reviewed and released separately.

options.title: Defer canonical migration
options.body: Keep the current accessor seam and postpone the SQLite-only runtime switch until the upgrade and rollback contract is safer.

recommendation.title: Approve after all gates
recommendation.body: Accept the one-way contract after unrelated changes and exact-head defects are removed and final-head upgrade, restart, continuity, archive, recovery, and downgrade proof is published.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main provenance and the strongest contribution history across the canonical storage and SDK paths make this the best available decision owner.
